title: DoW Solicitations Move to PIEE: BD Pipeline Guide October 2026
summary: Learn what the October 2026 DoW shift to PIEE means for registration, roles, and monitoring, plus how GovDash keeps your BD pipeline unified.
body_markdown:
If you track DoW opportunities and haven't set up a PIEE account yet, October 1, 2026 is the date that matters. DOD's mandate moves unclassified DoW solicitation packages, Q&A releases, and submission portals to the PIEE Solicitation Module, and SAM.gov alone won't get your team to the finish line anymore. Getting registered, assigning the right roles, and pointing your monitoring process at PIEE before a solicitation drops is what keeps your pipeline intact.


**TLDR:**


- DOD mandates PIEE Solicitation Module for all unclassified DoW solicitations starting October 1, 2026. Register at piee.eb.mil before a solicitation drops or you cannot submit.


- SAM.gov only carries notice-level data now. Full packages, amendments, and Q&A windows live in PIEE, so a SAM.gov-only workflow creates real submission gaps.


- You need the Proposal Manager role to submit. Proposal View Only looks similar in the interface but cannot submit anything.


- Most submission failures trace to setup gaps: inactive CAM accounts, missing CAGE Code links, wrong roles, non-searchable PDFs, and expired CAC certificates.


- GovDash surfaces PIEE-sourced DoW solicitations directly in the GovDash pipeline alongside SAM.gov, keeping your BD pipeline in one place across all three source types.


## What the DOD PIEE Mandate Actually Says


Starting October 1, 2026, contracting officers across DOD are required to use the PIEE Solicitation Module for publishing unclassified solicitations and receiving offers and quotes. The mandate, issued under[PGI 205.1](https://www.acquisition.gov/dfarspgi/pgi-205.1-dissemination-information) , applies DOD-wide unless specific exceptions apply. The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport flagged the change as a[major procedural shift](https://discover.govdash.com/solicitations/019ef4bd-2f88-70ca-bc90-f17bf11326a1--mandatory-use-of-piee-solicitation-module-effective-1-october-2026) for industry. Vendors must be registered at[piee.eb.mil](https://piee.eb.mil/) to respond to any covered solicitation. Missing that registration means missing the submission window, regardless of proposal quality.


## What PIEE Is and Why DOD Chose It


PIEE stands for Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment. It is[DOD's primary enterprise purchase-to-pay application](https://piee.eb.mil/) , with companies reporting over $7.1 billion in spending across the department and its supporting agencies.


Most contractors have touched PIEE before, just not for proposals. The Wide Area Workflow (WAWF) module handles invoicing and payment, so if you've submitted an invoice to a federal customer, you've already logged in. The Solicitation Module is a separate function within the same system, built for pre-award activity: publishing solicitations, receiving offers, and managing quote submissions.


DOD's rationale for consolidating under PIEE is straightforward. A single portal means more automated intake, controlled access, and fewer gaps in how solicitation documents and vendor responses are captured. Standardization reduces the manual coordination that previously varied by agency and contracting office.


## What DoW Solicitations Moving to PIEE Means in Practice


Starting October 1, unclassified DoW solicitations and their amendments publish through the PIEE Solicitation Module. Offers and quotes go back through the same system.[SAM.gov](https://www.govdash.com/glossary/sam-gov-(system-for-award-management)) may still carry notice-level announcements, but the actual solicitation documents, Q&A releases, and submission portals live at piee.eb.mil.


The practical consequences run deeper than a new login. Teams monitoring SAM.gov for full solicitation packages may now find shell notices pointing to PIEE for attachments. Amendment tracking moves there too: scope changes, Q&A postings, and deadline extensions flow through PIEE, so a BD team checking only SAM.gov could miss a change that disqualifies a non-conforming offer.


Email and agency-specific upload portals are no longer valid submission routes for covered solicitations. The Proposal Manager role in PIEE is the only authorized submission path.


For capture and proposal teams, three things must be in place before a solicitation drops:


- An active PIEE account with current user credentials, so your team can access solicitation documents the moment they post.


- A registered Proposal Manager role, which is the only role authorized to submit offers through the PIEE Proposal Manager module.


- A monitoring process that watches PIEE directly, instead of depending entirely on SAM.gov alerts, as part of a broader approach to[tracking opportunity lifecycle across multiple sources](https://www.govdash.com/playbook/track-opportunity-lifecycle-across-multiple-sources) .


## How to Register for a PIEE Account: The Step-by-Step Process


The[official PIEE vendor getting started guide](https://piee.eb.mil/xhtml/unauth/web/homepage/vendorGettingStartedHelp.xhtml) outlines five required steps before your team can respond to any covered solicitation:


1. Register with SAM.gov (mandatory)


2. Add your CAGE Code to the PIEE Vendor Group Structure (one-time required step)


3. Designate a Contractor Administrator (CAM)


4. Have the CAM self-register in PIEE (mandatory, as the CAM activates all other users)


5. Add additional roles and users


Once the CAM is active, individual users can self-register. Two roles apply to proposal work: Proposal View Only (can search solicitations and view offers) and Proposal Manager (required to actually submit an offer). Anyone responsible for submitting needs the Proposal Manager role, not view access alone.


## The Proposal Manager Role: Permissions and Responsibilities


The Proposal Manager role is the only role in PIEE authorized to take action on a solicitation. According to the[PIEE Solicitation Module training documentation](https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/xhtml/wbt/sol/solicitation/proposals.xhtml) , a Proposal Manager can indicate interest, post or withdraw an offer, submit unsolicited proposals, manage saved searches, save draft offers, and track submitted ones across pursuits.


Proposal View Only users can search solicitations, look up NAICS and PSC codes, and view submitted offers, but cannot submit anything. If someone on your team will touch the submit button at any point, they need the Proposal Manager role.


Capability Proposal Manager Proposal View Only


Search solicitations ✓ ✓


Look up NAICS and PSC codes ✓ ✓


View submitted offers ✓ ✓


Indicate interest in a solicitation ✓ ✗


Save draft offers ✓ ✗


Post or withdraw an offer ✓ ✗


Submit unsolicited proposals ✓ ✗


Manage saved searches ✓ ✗


Track submitted offers across pursuits ✓ ✗


A practical way to divide access: BD analysts monitoring the pipeline can operate under Proposal View Only, while capture leads and anyone coordinating final submission need Proposal Manager access. Because account activation runs through your CAM, confirm your CAM is active before a solicitation drops and the clock starts.


## How to Find and Monitor DoW Solicitations Inside PIEE


Once registered with an active Proposal Manager role, finding relevant solicitations, including the eventual[request for proposal](https://www.govdash.com/glossary/rfp-meaning) , in PIEE depends on how well you configure the system upfront.


The PIEE Solicitation Module supports notice search filtering by agency, NAICS code, PSC code, and solicitation status. Users can flag specific notices and create saved searches to monitor recurring opportunity types without manually re-running filters each session. Saved searches and flagged notices are part of the core Proposal Manager dashboard, available the moment your role is active.


The practical difference between passive and proactive monitoring matters here. Amendments and Q&A releases post directly through the module, so a saved search tied to your relevant NAICS or agency filters keeps your team current without a daily manual pull.


A few habits worth building from day one:


- Save searches by NAICS code, PSC code, and issuing office relevant to your DoW pursuit areas.


- Flag active solicitations so they appear on your dashboard without re-filtering.


- Review your notification settings after setup so amendments trigger alerts, as well as initial postings.


## How to Submit a Proposal Through the PIEE Solicitation Module


Submitting through PIEE follows a fixed sequence. Log in at piee.eb.mil using a CAC, PIV card, or user ID and password. From the Solicitation Module, search for the relevant solicitation, open the offer submission interface, and complete the offer identifier field before attaching your files.


Before building your[compliance matrix](https://www.govdash.com/glossary/what-is-a-compliance-matrix) and assembling files, note that file naming follows a required convention: Solicitation Number_FIRM NAME. Per the PIEE Solicitation Module FAQ, files must be in native format (.doc, .xls, .ppt) or searchable PDF. Scanned flat PDFs that are not searchable are a common rejection point. The portal enforces the posted deadline without exception, and a government-controlled system will not accept a late file regardless of technical difficulty on your end.


Two practical notes before submission day: confirm browser compatibility, as PIEE has documented requirements around supported browsers, and verify your CAC or PIV card certificate is current. Certificate expirations have caused last-minute login failures that no amount of proposal quality can fix after the deadline passes.


## Common Errors That Cause Failed or Late Submissions


Most submission failures trace back to setup gaps, not proposal quality. Check each of these before the solicitation posts:


- CAM account inactive or expired: every user activation runs through your CAM, so if that account lapses, no one can be added or reactivated.


- CAGE Code not linked to the PIEE Vendor Group Structure: registration without this step leaves role assignment failing silently.


- Wrong Proposal Manager role: Proposal View Only looks similar in the interface but cannot submit, so verify the role explicitly before solicitation day.


- File naming errors: PIEE requires Solicitation Number_FIRM NAME, and deviating from that convention can cause validation failure.


- Non-searchable PDFs: scanned flat files are rejected, so all PDFs must be text-searchable.


- Browser incompatibility: running an unsupported browser causes authentication and upload failures.


- Expired CAC or PIV certificate: expiration on submission day has no workaround once the deadline passes.


## How This Affects Your BD Pipeline Beyond Registration


Registration is a one-time setup. The harder adjustment is rebuilding how your team monitors, tracks, and acts on DoW opportunities going forward.


If your BD process routes SAM.gov alerts into a pipeline tracker, that workflow now captures only partial data. Full solicitation packages, amendments, and Q&A windows for covered DoW solicitations live in PIEE. A team depending solely on SAM.gov notifications may see the notice but miss the Q&A that changes scope, or the amendment that moves the deadline.


Go through your active DoW pursuits now, ideally before a notice even posts by[forecasting opportunities before the RFP drops](https://www.govdash.com/blog/find-the-contract-before-the-rfp-drops) , and flag which ones will release or continue under the October 1 mandate. For each, confirm your monitoring process points to PIEE directly, and not to SAM.gov alone, as part of a broader effort, see[GovDash for defense contractors](https://www.govdash.com/defense) . Any opportunity tracked without a PIEE source reference is a gap worth closing before a solicitation drops.

The registration steps are straightforward, but the real work is rebuilding how your team monitors and tracks DOW opportunities going forward. SAM.gov alone won't give you the full picture once covered solicitations move through PIEE. ## FAQ


### What does the PIEE proposal submission mandate mean for DoW contractors who currently track solicitations through SAM.gov?


Starting October 1, 2026, SAM.gov may carry only notice-level announcements for covered DOD solicitations, while the actual documents, Q&A releases, and submission portals live at piee.eb.mil. A BD team monitoring only SAM.gov could see the notice but miss an amendment that alters scope or a Q&A posting that changes the deadline, leaving a non-conforming offer with no recovery path.


### How do I register for a PIEE account and set up the Proposal Manager role before a DoW solicitation drops?


Registration requires five steps: verify SAM.gov registration, add your CAGE Code to the PIEE Vendor Group Structure, designate a Contractor Administrator (CAM), have the CAM self-register in PIEE, then add individual users with the correct role. Anyone touching the submit button needs the Proposal Manager role, not Proposal View Only, since View Only cannot submit offers regardless of how far along the pursuit is.


### Should I use GovDash or check PIEE directly to monitor DoW solicitations after the October 1 mandate?


PIEE is a native public source in GovDash, sitting alongside SAM.gov and SLED sources, so covered DOD solicitations surface in your tracking workflow without a separate monitoring setup. The practical case for consolidating is speed: teams checking PIEE, SAM.gov, and SLED separately across three portals will miss connections that a single pipeline catches, and customers using GovDash have identified 150% more weekly opportunities by keeping pipeline intelligence in one place.


### What makes a GovCon-specific AI system different from a general-purpose AI tool like ChatGPT for PIEE proposal submission workflows?


General-purpose AI can draft text from a pasted solicitation, but it has no GovCon data model: no FAR/DFARS clause library, no past performance schema, and no audit trail showing which uploaded document supported a given statement. A GovCon-specific system maps Sections L and M to requirements, keeps a compliance matrix that updates when an amendment drops, and matches requirements against your contract history with citations. Each output traces to a source record in your Data Library, which matters when a contracting officer questions your basis of estimate or compliance mapping.


### What are the most common reasons a PIEE proposal submission fails or gets rejected?


Most failures trace back to seven setup gaps: an inactive or expired CAM account, a CAGE Code not linked to the PIEE Vendor Group Structure, the wrong role assigned (Proposal View Only instead of Proposal Manager), file names that do not follow the Solicitation Number_FIRM NAME convention, scanned flat PDFs that are not text-searchable, unsupported browsers causing authentication failures, and expired CAC or PIV certificates that block login after the deadline has passed.
